LIAs / LIMs
ComponentsComparisonsEvaluation guidePaper

Approximate adders and multipliers

LIA and LIM are libraries of imprecise arithmetic components for studying accuracy–cost trade-offs. Select an architecture, operand width, and LPL setting; compare its numerical error and available hardware measurements, then download the corresponding C, Python, or Verilog RTL model.

Reconfigurable Imprecision
LIA adders and LIM multipliers allow users to configure the imprecision level through LPL, which determines how many least-significant bits are approximated. For example, in an 8-bit addition with a 9-bit result, LPL=4 means that the four least-significant bits are implemented using approximate logic. Similarly, for an 8×8 multiplication with a 16-bit result, LPL=8 means that the eight least-significant product bits are approximated. The provided 8-bit LIM models also support smaller LPL values.
Exploring Imprecision with Lower Hardware-Cost Variation
Compared with the evaluated EvoApprox circuits, LIA and LIM designs show smaller variations in area and power, particularly for LIM. This makes them useful for investigating the impact of imprecision on application accuracy while reducing the influence of hardware-cost differences. However, area and power are not constant across configurations, and comparisons depend on the evaluation setup.
Consistent Mean Error Across Different LPLs
Some LIA and LIM architectures maintain the same value of specific error criteria across different imprecision levels. For example, LOA (lia_05) maintains an ME of +0.25 using the approximate − exact convention (−0.25 using exact − approximate). This behavior is verified under exhaustive uniform input evaluation for the tested configurations. However, other error metrics, such as MAE and MSE, may still change as LPL increases.
Architectures Optimized for Different Error Metrics
LIA and LIM provide different architectures designed to target specific error metrics, including ME, MAE, MSE, and PE. Each architecture is identified by its optimization objective, allowing users to select and compare designs based on their application requirements. This also enables investigating how different error characteristics affect application-level accuracy and exploring trade-offs between computational error and hardware cost.

Significant Note: The LIA/LIM architectures and original C libraries are the work of the ICVLSI research group at Shahid Beheshti University, Tehran, Iran. This website was developed by Gelara, a group member and not an author of the original paper. Gelara prepared the other implementation versions, validated them, and provided the Yosys/OpenROAD synthesis information and comparisons.

Numerical error. For e = approximate − exact: ME = mean(e), MSE = mean(e²), MAE = mean(|e|), PE = fraction(e ≠ 0). Min/max are signed extrema; worst absolute error = max(|min|, |max|). Error uses output units; MSE uses output units²; PE is a fraction from 0 to 1.

PPA. Area and power retain the source CSV’s µm² and total µW at the supplied benchmark settings. The maintainer reports Yosys/ABC mapping to Nangate45 and pre-layout OpenSTA within OpenROAD with identical timing, loading, and switching-activity assumptions; see the comparison methodology. Tool versions, corner, numerical constraints/activity, and timing-path definition were not supplied. † Timing retains delay_ns verbatim; negative values are not physical propagation delays. Missing measurements are shown as a dash.

One width and LPL are shown at a time. Numerical metrics were checked exhaustively against C; reports and full-precision values record the tested domain. CSV signed errors were converted from exact − approximate and checked against C; PPA values were not copied to other LPLs. Import findings.

Numerical error. For e = approximate − exact: ME = mean(e), MSE = mean(e²), MAE = mean(|e|), PE = fraction(e ≠ 0). Min/max are signed extrema; worst absolute error = max(|min|, |max|). Error uses output units; MSE uses output units²; PE is a fraction from 0 to 1.

PPA. Area and power retain the source CSV’s µm² and total µW at the supplied benchmark settings. The maintainer reports Yosys/ABC mapping to Nangate45 and pre-layout OpenSTA within OpenROAD with identical timing, loading, and switching-activity assumptions; see the comparison methodology. Tool versions, corner, numerical constraints/activity, and timing-path definition were not supplied. † Timing retains delay_ns verbatim; negative values are not physical propagation delays. Missing measurements are shown as a dash.

One width and LPL are shown at a time. Numerical metrics were checked exhaustively against C; reports and full-precision values record the tested domain. CSV signed errors were converted from exact − approximate and checked against C; PPA values were not copied to other LPLs. Import findings.

LIA / LIM and EvoApprox: area, power and timing

Six plots from the supplied comparison CSVs. Each curve sorts one library’s circuits independently by the plotted value; the horizontal axis is within-library percentile, not LPL. These benchmarks all use LPL = 8 for LIA or LIM.

Synthesis and characterization. All adder and multiplier architectures in these comparisons are synthesized using Yosys with ABC technology mapping, targeting the Nangate45 standard-cell library. Pre-layout timing and power are evaluated using OpenSTA within OpenROAD under identical timing, loading, and switching-activity assumptions across architectures. This methodology is reported by the maintainer.

Exhaustive functional verification. At LPL=8, C and RTL agree for all 262,144 ordered pairs of two unsigned 9-bit operands (512 × 512) per LIA adder, and all 65,536 ordered pairs of two unsigned 8-bit operands (256 × 256) per LIM multiplier. See the LIA report and LIM report. EvoApprox verification flags are retained as reported in the source CSVs.

Published synthesis results. Consult the original LIA/LIM paper, EvoApprox8b paper, and EvoApproxLib extension paper for their experiments and characterization contexts. The plots here use the supplied comparison CSVs and the flow described above.

9-bit LIA, LPL=8 vs. EvoApprox 8-bit + MSB

Source comparison CSV. Negative timing values are retained; their physical meaning is unresolved.

8-bit LIM, LPL=8 vs. EvoApprox 8-bit

Source comparison CSV. Missing PPA measurements: mul8u_TD3; omitted from the relevant curves. The timing-path definition was not supplied.

The common flow and identical assumptions are maintainer-reported; tool versions, exact Liberty corner, voltage, temperature, numerical timing/loading/activity settings, and original analysis reports were not supplied. Reported timing is retained verbatim; negative values are not interpreted as physical propagation delays. Import findings · All plotted values and source rows (CSV)

Choose a configuration for your constraints

LPL and other parameters depend on the architecture. Use measured configurations to find candidates, then evaluate them with your inputs and hardware flow. A chosen error limit does not by itself determine area, power, or delay.

  1. Choose and download a configuration

    Filter the table by operation, operand width, and LPL. Download its standalone code, or a combined family file. To list the same configurations from the repository root, use Python 3:

    python tools/catalog.py validate
python tools/catalog.py select --kind adder --width 8 --lpl 4

    C and Python use the function names recorded in the row’s provenance. RTL uses the named top module with the selected N (operand width) and LPL. The multiplier software parameter VBL corresponds to RTL LPL.

  2. Reproduce the exhaustive error checks

    With Python 3 and GCC on your PATH, run the original C and Python implementations over every ordered pair of 8-bit inputs, for all seven LPL settings:

    python tools/validate_models.py --kind adder --width 8 --lpl 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
python tools/validate_models.py --kind multiplier --width 8 --lpl 1 2 3 4 5 6 7

# Additional settings used in the supplied comparisons
python tools/validate_models.py --kind adder --width 9 --lpl 8 --output result/validation/adder9-lpl8-c-python.json
python tools/validate_models.py --kind multiplier --width 8 --lpl 8 --output result/validation/multiplier8-lpl8-c-python.json

    Reports contain per-input mismatch counts, ME, MSE, MAE, PE, signed min/max, exact rational aggregates, and a separately reported 0–127 operand subset. See the saved validation results. Agreement establishes implementation consistency within this domain.

    Evaluate a different input workload

    Export matching exact and approximate integer outputs to a CSV with exact,approximate column headers. Replace the paths below with your files:

    python tools/measure_errors.py --input path/to/output-pairs.csv --output path/to/error.json

    Each row has equal weight, including duplicates. Record the operand domain, workload, configuration, and testbench separately; exhaustive coverage is not inferred from CSV length.

  3. Measure area, power, and delay

    Synthesize the supplied RTL at the selected parameters and run your physical and timing flow. Record the standard-cell library and corner, tool versions, constraints, activity assumptions, and report definitions.

    Available measurements. The supplied CSVs provide area, power, and reported timing for 9-bit LIA at LPL=8 and 8-bit LIM at LPL=8. The maintainer reports Yosys/ABC mapping to Nangate45, followed by pre-layout OpenSTA analysis within OpenROAD under common timing, loading, and switching assumptions. The scripts, exact Liberty corner, numerical settings, and timing-path definitions were not supplied, so the complete PPA command sequence cannot yet be reproduced. See the methodology and import findings.

    A different library, timing target, placement, or switching activity requires a new characterization context.

  4. Filter measured candidates

    Use the table’s limits or run the selection command below. The numbers are example search constraints, not circuit measurements or promised targets. Adjust them to your requirements.

    python tools/catalog.py select --kind adder --width 9 --lpl 8 --max-mae 50 --max-area-um2 20 --max-power-uw 5

    Use --kind multiplier for LIM. Use --max-mse, --max-abs-me, or --max-abs-error for other error criteria. Use --max-delay-ns only for confirmed physical delay; raw reported timing does not satisfy that constraint. Unknown measurements are excluded when a corresponding limit is set.

    The command returns existing catalog entries. Generating or tuning a new architecture requires its implementation and evaluation tools, which are not included here.

Regenerate the model downloads and catalog

After the base and additional C/Python/RTL validation checks pass, regenerate the models, import the comparison data and plots, verify the packaged code, then build the catalog and archives. Plot generation requires Matplotlib:

python -m pip install -r requirements-plots.txt
python tools/prepare_models.py --kind adder
python tools/prepare_models.py --kind multiplier
python tools/import_comparisons.py
python tools/check_packaged_models.py --kind adder
python tools/check_packaged_models.py --kind multiplier
python tools/catalog.py build
python tools/summarize_validation.py

Model preparation checks that the original sources still match their validation reports. See the dataset guide for provenance and PPA requirements.

Paper and attribution

The original LIA/LIM architectures are attributed to Mohammad Haji Seyed Javadi, Mohsen Faryabi, and Hamid Reza Mahdiani. This site organizes implementations and characterization data for those architectures.

M. H. S. Javadi, M. Faryabi, and H. R. Mahdiani. A Comprehensive Model for Efficient Design Space Exploration of Imprecise Computational Blocks. ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems, 2023.

EvoApprox Library:

V. Mrazek, R. Hrbacek, Z. Vasicek, and L. Sekanina. EvoApprox8b: Library of Approximate Adders and Multipliers for Circuit Design and Benchmarking of Approximation Methods. DATE, 2017. Author-hosted PDF.

V. Mrazek, Z. Vasicek, and L. Sekanina. EvoApproxLib: Extended Library of Approximate Arithmetic Circuits. WOSET, 2019.

Published measurements have their own characterization conditions. In particular, the original EvoApprox8b study uses a TSMC 180 nm context (sections III–IV), rather than this comparison’s Nangate45 flow. The plots retain the supplied CSV values. Methodology and measurement provenance.

Cite the original paper when using the architectures, and the relevant repository release when using packaged models or new measurements. A release identifier and source-code license have not been supplied.
